title: Health Records UI for baseline labs & vitals tracking

requirements.summary: Add an authenticated Health Records UI where users can add and view personal lab/vitals track record entries (hemoglobin, platelets, BP systolic, BP diastolic) in English.
acceptanceCriteria: App includes a reachable Health Records page or section while logged in.
The UI provides an “Add Record” form that supports: Hemoglobin, Platelets, Blood Pressure (High/Systolic), Blood Pressure (Low/Diastolic).
The form collects value and date (and unit if not implied) and prevents submission with invalid/empty values, showing an English validation message.
After saving, the new record appears in the records list without requiring a full page refresh (React Query invalidation/refetch pattern).
The records list shows type, value + unit, and date, sorted newest-first.

file_operations.description: Create an authenticated Health Records page with an English “Add Record” form (metric type selector + numeric value + date + unit display where applicable) and a newest-first records list rendering type, value+unit, and date. Compose existing shadcn/ui components (do not edit frontend/src/components/ui). Use the authorization component’s frontend guidance to ensure this page only appears for signed-in users and to handle backend authorization errors gracefully. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Add React Query hooks for Health Records: (1) query to fetch the caller’s records list, and (2) mutation to add a new record, with React Query invalidation/refetch so newly saved records appear without a full refresh. Ensure errors (including authorization traps) are surfaced as small English messages/toasts. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Update the frontend backend interface typings to match the new backend capabilities for creating and listing per-user health track record entries (including date/day identifier, metric type, value, and unit where applicable), so the Health Records hooks/page can call the new backend functions in a type-safe way.

requirements.summary: Add logged-in navigation entry points to Health Records using the existing TanStack Router pattern without disrupting existing flows.
acceptanceCriteria: There is a visible navigation entry point to Health Records from the logged-in UI (e.g., header nav and/or dashboard quick action).
Navigation uses the existing TanStack Router route setup pattern in frontend/src/App.tsx.
All user-facing labels for the new navigation item and page are in English.

file_operations.description: Register a new TanStack Router route for the Health Records page (e.g., /health-records) using the existing createRoute + routeTree.addChildren pattern, ensuring it remains behind the existing AuthGate (signed-in experience).
Add an English navigation button/link for “Health Records” to the existing logged-in header navigation, following the current Button-based nav pattern and keeping existing items unchanged.

Add a small, non-disruptive English entry point (e.g., a secondary button or compact card action) that navigates to the Health Records route from the dashboard while preserving existing dashboard, logging, scanning, chat, and install flows.

requirements.summary: Show a compact read-only Baseline Health summary card (latest hemoglobin/platelets/BP systolic/BP diastolic) in a consistently visible logged-in location with graceful failure handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard (or another consistently visible logged-in location) shows a compact “Baseline Health” summary when at least one record exists.
The summary displays the latest available value for each metric type; missing metrics are either omitted or shown as “Not set” (English).
If the snapshot query fails, the UI degrades gracefully (no app crash) and shows a small English fallback message (e.g., “Could not load baseline health data”).

file_operations.description: Create a React Query hook to fetch the caller’s baseline snapshot from the backend (latest per metric), returning structured loading/error state. Ensure failures are handled without throwing UI-breaking errors and provide a clear English fallback state. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Implement a compact, read-only “Baseline Health” summary card component that displays latest values for hemoglobin, platelets, BP systolic, and BP diastolic when present; show missing metrics as “Not set” (English) or omit them; and show an English fallback message if the snapshot query fails. Compose existing shadcn/ui components (do not edit frontend/src/components/ui).

Wire the BaselineHealthCard into the dashboard in a compact, consistently visible section, rendering it only when at least one baseline metric exists and ensuring the dashboard remains stable even if the snapshot fails to load.
Update baseline snapshot typings (if needed) to reflect the dedicated backend query used for the Baseline Health card, ensuring the snapshot data can represent missing metrics without trapping.
